calibration_rulings.title: Homographs and the helmet: «الظفر», «الجفر», «فوجی خود».
calibration_rulings.binds: dhafar-museum::title, body; najim-museum::summary, body, area; dar-alturath::body (b9: change 0; b17: the helmet, «آہنی ٹوپیاں»). Every later war helmet.
calibration_rulings.ruling: (1) «الظفر» and (2) «الجفر»: A, no fence. No ruling fences a family name (N122, whose open question to the owner now names «الظفر» too); «جفر» is no common Urdu word, so N73 (2) does not reach «الجفر». The reader read both as names without a remark. (3) THE HELMET: B, «جنگی خود», on the reader: he read «فوجی خود» as 'the military themselves' (item 4, moderate), the case stage 4 named for B. «جنگی خود» is the dictionary's collocation (rekhta's helmet page) and «جنگی» is never a noun 'soldier'. C, the loan «ہیلمٹ», stays refused (P16: a native word exists). Change 0. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-14) AS AN OWNER DECISION, OPEN (the judge file gives this entry the status "ruled"; in the list for the owner, its decision 8 adds a name of this entry, item (1), to the open question of N122 (family names read as words), which this ruling cites; N122 itself is a ruling of b8 and is not amended here; it is entered with its open question stated, as b6 entered N93, N94 and N99, b7 entered N106 and N110 and b8 entered N122, N129 and N130). The wording ruled above is what the text carries until the owner answers; no leaf waits on the answer. THE QUESTION, as the list for the owner in the judge file words it (its note FOR THE OWNER, decision 8): «الظفر» joins N122's family-name homograph question. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-14) AS AN OWNER DECISION, OPEN, FROM THE JUDGE'S ADDENDUM (the addendum to judge round 1, written after the proof pass on round 1 and the second blind reader, changes no string and no ruling; its list for the owner, section 6, holds what that reader added or sharpened and keeps round 1's list; its item 1 is the question this ruling concerns, and its section 2 note 6 asks that item (3) of this ruling be entered with the contest stated; entered with its question stated, as b8 entered N122, N129 and N130). The wording ruled above is what the text carries until the owner answers; no leaf waits on the answer. THE CONTEST, as the addendum words it (section 2, note 6): two readers of two read «خود» first as 'self' («فوجی خود», then «جنگی خود»); both recovered the helmet on a second look. THE CANDIDATES, as the addendum lists them (section 3, change 0): (a) «جنگی خود (آہنی ٹوپیاں)», reader 2's wording. It brings a meaning bracket after a common noun, a form no ruling has (P3c point 5 keeps two bracket forms, both for names). It would be the first such bracket on /ur/ and needs a ruling, not a batch edit. (b) the loan «ہیلمٹ», reader 1's bracket: refused under P16, since a native word exists. (c) a description such as «سر کی حفاظت کے لیے پہنے جانے والے جنگی خود» or «لوہے کی جنگی ٹوپیاں». The first is wordy and still says «خود». The second adds 'iron', which neither source says. (d) «کلاہ آہنی» (rekhta's definition word): literary, and it says 'iron' too. As the addendum rules there: «جنگی خود» stays, charged once more under dar-alturath nativeness. The candidates (a) to (d) go to the owner (section 6). The N139 (3) entry on apply states the contest. THE QUESTION, as the addendum words it (section 6, item 1): The helmet: two readers of two read «خود» first as 'self'. The options are the meaning bracket «جنگی خود (آہنی ٹوپیاں)» (a new form, needs a ruling), the loan «ہیلمٹ» (his P16 refuses it while a native word exists), or a description. The text keeps «جنگی خود» until he answers. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-14), proof pass on round 1, note 5, and the judge's addendum, section 2 note 5, record only (no string moves): the candidate list of this entry in the judge file, which the termbase does not carry, labels candidate A "(in the text)", but the helmet it quotes, «فوجی خود», is withdrawn and no longer stands in the text (item (3) of the ruling takes B); the names it quotes, «صالح الظفر» and «الجفر», stay, as items (1) and (2) of the ruling take A; the label reads "(stage 4's text)", the smallest correction the addendum words (as b8 proof on round 2, note 6). The ruling above says what replaced it. The proof pass also notes that the evidence of this entry, which the termbase does not carry either, still quotes the replaced sentence in the present tense. ‖ AMENDED IN b17 (judge round 1, 2026-10-15; OWNER DECIDED 2026-10-15 (DECISIONS «Owner's answers on 2026-10-15»: "N139 helmet: «آہنی ٹوپی» (replaces «جنگی خود»)"); item N270 A): ITEM (3), THE HELMET, IS ANSWERED: a war helmet is «آہنی ٹوپی» (feminine by «ٹوپی», rekhta «اسم، مؤنث»; «آہنی» an invariable adjective; plural «آہنی ٹوپیاں»), the owner's wording, chosen from the candidates the b9 addendum sent him. dar-alturath body (b17): «ہتھیاروں میں تلواریں اور آہنی ٹوپیاں ہیں، جن میں سے بعض تین سو برس سے زیادہ پرانی ہیں۔» (agreement «پرانی», both nouns feminine). B «جنگی خود» is withdrawn and stands nowhere; «فوجی خود» and «ہیلمٹ» stay unwritten. COST, recorded and not reopened: «آہنی» says 'iron', which neither source says, and the source's 'military' is carried by the frame «ہتھیاروں میں», not by the noun; the compound is unattested on ur.wikipedia — the owner's decision makes the form. The on-05 reader of b17 read the sentence without a remark (item 39). Items (1) and (2) (the names «الظفر», «الجفر») and their open question under N122 are unchanged. The guard is amended to the decided form and machine-read (tested: b17/s7-guard.out.txt).

calibration_rulings.title: 'Bedouin' (of the women who sell): «بدو», «صحرا نشین» or «بادیہ نشین»?
calibration_rulings.binds: women-souq::body, faq[2].a; the key «بادیہ نشین» (retires «بدو»). Every later mention of the Bedouin on /ur/.
calibration_rulings.ruling: C («بادیہ نشین», stage 4's letter; the fallback round 1 named), ROUND 2. THE TWO READERS: the first (on-05) read «شہری بھی اور بدو بھی» in body and faq[2].a with no remark; the second (on-r1, item 6, moderate) heard «بدو» as 'mildly dismissive ("uncouth")' in a respectful line about women sellers — exactly the trigger stage 4 named ('if a reader hears contempt or "uncouth" in «بدو», the judge replaces it by «بادیہ نشین» in both leaves') and round 1 kept. One reader of two, but the cost is the worst a word can do on this page, and the references carry it (ur.wikipedia's own lead of «بدو», rekhta's «بدوی» 'uncouth'). «بادیہ نشین» is neutral in the reference («عرب کے بادیہ نشین قبائل», 7 pages, HTTP 200, stage 4); the pair stays two nouns of a kind. The reader's «صحرائی (بدوی)» brings «بدوی» back; «بادیہ کی» unbalances the pair. Changes 0, 1; UNREAD — the next reader tests it. The key «بدو» is RETIRED. B «صحرا نشین» stays refused (rekhta: 'hermit'). ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-14) AS AN OWNER DECISION, OPEN (the judge file gives this entry the status "ruled"; its list for the owner puts the question this ruling concerns; entered with its question stated, as b8, b9 and b10 entered theirs). The wording ruled above is what the text carries until the owner answers; no leaf waits on the answer. THE QUESTION, as the list for the owner in the judge file words it (its note FOR THE OWNER, item 2): women-souq: 'Bedouin' is now «بادیہ نشین» on /ur/ — a reader heard «بدو» as dismissive; say if you prefer another word ‖ ADDENDUM (b11, round 2): the third reader (on-r2, item 8, minor) read «بادیہ نشین» in body and faq[2].a: "bookish and Persianized. I understood it, but it is not how one speaks of people today" — meaning taken, no tone fault; three readers in all: «بدو» passed by the first, 'uncouth' to the second, «بادیہ نشین» understood and called bookish by the third. C stands; its register cost is charged on women-souq. ‖ AMENDED IN b17 (judge round 1, 2026-10-15; OWNER DECIDED 2026-10-15 (DECISIONS «Owner's answers on 2026-10-15»: "women-souq sellers: local women of Al-Ahsa. TO DO: EN 'townswomen' corrected to match the Arabic «محليّات»; the Urdu keeps «بادیہ نشین» where the Arabic keeps Bedouin and town women"), carried into the source by #175 (EN "both local women and Bedouin"; AR «محليّاتٌ وبدويات», unchanged); items N266 A, N267 A): THE QUESTION ('say if you prefer another word') IS ANSWERED: «بادیہ نشین» stays. THE PAIR (b17): «مقامی بھی اور بادیہ نشین بھی» in women-souq body and faq[2].a — «مقامی» the Arabic's «محليّات»; «شہری» (the old English 'townswomen') has left the pair. COST on record: rekhta gives «شہری» as the opposite of «بادیہ نشین»; with «مقامی» a reader may ask whether the Bedouin women are not local too, as the Arabic invites; the on-05 reader of b17 did not ask, and called «بادیہ نشین» bookish (item 26, minor; the third reader to say so), charged on women-souq. The guard's first clause is kept letter for letter; the proofreader's clause now names the pair the text carries and is machine-read (tested: b17/s7-guard.out.txt).
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker: the retired key «بدو» does not occur. For the proofreader and the stage checker: none of «شہری بھی اور بادیہ نشین», «صحرا نشین», «بدوی» occurs; «بادیہ نشین» stands in the pair with «مقامی» («مقامی بھی اور بادیہ نشین بھی»).

calibration_rulings.title: 'Countryside chalets' («أكواخ ريفية»): «دیہی جھونپڑیاں» or «دیہی کٹیائیں»?
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «دیہی جھونپڑیاں», feminine plural — the Arabic authority's own noun. COST, charged on accuracy, nativeness and fit: the reader read 'shabby huts' before the setting told him they are rustic chalets (item 18, moderate) — the cost stage 4 named. Not changed: B «کٹیا» is unverified and as humble; the loan «کاٹیج» is refused (P16); his 'rooms' changes the thing; 'rural-style huts' would add a claim of style that neither source makes. ON RECORD for the next reader of this page: if a second reader also reads shacks, the judge weighs «دیہی طرز کی جھونپڑیاں» against the cost of 'style'. EN 'chalets' against AR 'huts' is logged for the owner. ‖ ROUND 2: Unchanged: the second reader made no remark on «جھونپڑیاں» (one reader of two read shacks); the fallback condition ('a second reader also reads shacks') is not met. Cost stays charged on zaki-alsalem-farm. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-14) AS AN OWNER DECISION, OPEN (the judge file gives this entry the status "ruled"; its list for the owner puts the question this ruling concerns; entered with its question stated, as b8, b9 and b10 entered theirs). The wording ruled above is what the text carries until the owner answers; no leaf waits on the answer. THE QUESTION, as the list for the owner in the judge file words it (its note FOR THE OWNER, item 4): zaki-alsalem-farm: 'chalets' (EN) or 'huts' (AR)? (N175) ‖ ADDENDUM (b11, round 2): the third reader (on-r2, item 17, moderate) read «دیہی جھونپڑیاں» as poor shacks and offered «دیہاتی طرز کی جھونپڑیاں»; two readers of three. The condition round 1 set is met and was weighed: 'rural-style' would add a claim of design that neither source makes (AR rural huts, EN countryside chalets), so A stands; the cost is charged once on each of accuracy, nativeness and fit of zaki-alsalem-farm; the owner's answer to 'chalets or huts' decides the word. ‖ AMENDED IN b17 (judge round 1, 2026-10-15; OWNER DECIDED 2026-10-15 (DECISIONS «Owner's answers on 2026-10-15»: "N175 zaki-alsalem-farm «اریاف»: traditional palm-frond huts"), carried into the source by #175 (EN "traditional palm-frond huts", AR «أكواخ تراثية من السعف»); items N264 A, N265 A): THE QUESTION ('chalets (EN) or huts (AR)?') IS ANSWERED: huts — the Arabic's noun, the one the text already had. THE WORDING (b17): «کھجور کے پتوں کی روایتی جھونپڑیاں» in zaki-alsalem-farm summary and body (feminine plural; «بھی ہیں», «بنائی گئی ہیں … کہلاتی ہیں» unchanged). «دیہی» has left the huts and stays only in the gloss of «“اریاف زکی”» (N170). The fallback «دیہی طرز کی جھونپڑیاں» is withdrawn with the old source wording. The 'shack' cost of b11 met the qualified noun on the on-05 reader of b17 with no remark (one reader). The guard gains a machine-read clause for the withdrawn wording (tested: b17/s7-guard.out.txt).
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader and the stage checker: «جھونپڑی» feminine; «کاٹیج» does not occur; «دیہی جھونپڑیاں» does not occur.

calibration_rulings.title: The frame of a P3b name met in running text with its generic ('countryside chalets known as Aryaf Zaki'): a naming clause or the «نامی» template?
calibration_rulings.binds: zaki-alsalem-farm::body; the key «اریاف زکی». Every later P3b name the source introduces with its generic and a naming verb.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: the generic first, the quoted name and its gloss in a naming clause — «… دیہی جھونپڑیاں بنائی گئی ہیں جو “اریاف زکی” (زکی کا دیہی علاقہ) کہلاتی ہیں۔» — the source's own 'known as', N107's frame. P3b's guard is met (marks at the one mention, the gloss once, straight after the closing mark) and P3b (3) is met by the generic standing as the antecedent of the clause that names it. The «نامی» template belongs to P15 (heritage villages) and P3c (2) (a «سوق» / «عین» name met in passing); role file 05 item 10's «نامی» clause is not owed where the generic already governs a naming clause, and B would stack «دیہی علاقہ) نامی دیہی». The reader: the marks and the bracket 'do work: I understood it is a name with a gloss' (item 19). B on record. ‖ ROUND 2: Unchanged; the second reader too read the marks and the bracket as a name and its gloss (item 17). EXCEPTION TO ROLE FILE 05, ITEM 10, for ap-meta to enter in this ruling's note: 'Role file 05, item 10, asks that a P3b name be followed, after its gloss, by «نامی» and its generic. Where the generic already stands as the antecedent of a naming clause («… جو “…” (…) کہلاتی ہیں», N107's frame), that clause discharges P3b (3) and the «نامی» clause is not owed; a proofreader applying item 10 reads it with this exception (b11, N170).' ‖ AMENDED IN b17 (judge round 1, 2026-10-15; owner N175, #175; item N273): the sentence quoted above is its rounds' history; the live sentence (b17) reads «… اس کے گرد کھجور کے پتوں کی روایتی جھونپڑیاں بنائی گئی ہیں جو “اریاف زکی” (زکی کا دیہی علاقہ) کہلاتی ہیں۔». The frame, the marks and the gloss are unchanged; the gloss renders the name «أرياف» (countryside), not the huts. COST, charged on zaki-alsalem-farm: with «دیہی» gone from the huts the gloss no longer echoes the noun, and the on-05 reader of b17 could not tell whether the name is the huts' or the bathing area's (item 17, moderate); the source names the huts ("huts known as 'Aryaf Zaki'"), so the Urdu keeps that. The ruling and its guard are unchanged. ‖ ROUND 2 (b17): the on-r1 reader too could not tell whether the name is the huts', the bathing area's or the farm's (item 17, moderate): two readers of two; charged; the owner's answer kept the name and its bracket.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader: «“اریاف زکی”» in marks at every mention, its gloss once straight after the closing mark; the generic that says what it is stands either as the antecedent of a naming clause («جو … کہلاتی ہیں») or after «نامی» — one of the two, not both.
calibration_rulings.ruled_by: Round 2 judge, b11 round 2, 2026-10-14; amended by the b17 judge, round 1, 2026-10-15

calibration_rulings.title: hamidiyah-souq, three leaves: "restored" / «رُمِّم» (#175, the owner's old building restored) — «مرمت» (A) or «بحال کیا گیا» (B)?
calibration_rulings.binds: hamidiyah-souq::summary, ::body, ::faq[2].a. Every later "restored" of a building.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «مرمت» — summary «جس کی مرمت … کی گئی», body and faq[2].a «… اس کی مرمت کی گئی». It is the approved /ur/ word for "restored" on seven pages (sahood, khuzam, baiah, jalaniyah, jabri-mosque, ameeriah …), the dictionaries give it the building sense with citations (udb 238286, rekhta), and «بحالی» is already the word of a different English ("rehabilitated"). CONFIRMED on the on-05 reader: no remark on «مرمت» in any of the three leaves, and his items 3, 9 and 10 show the building read as restored, not rebuilt. B refused: a second word for one English, leaning to 'reinstated'. Agreement: «مرمت» feminine (udb «امث») → «کی گئی». ‖ ROUND 2: the on-r1 reader too read the building as restored, no remark on «مرمت»; his item 14 (one project or several) is the sources'.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: "restored" is «مرمت» (feminine: «کی گئی»), "rehabilitated" «بحالی»; on hamidiyah-souq the building itself is not «دوبارہ تعمیر» (the reconstruction is Qaisariyah's).

calibration_rulings.title: hamidiyah-souq body and faq[2].a: after «… اس کی مرمت کی گئی», drop the two «بھی» (A) or keep the approved correlative (B)?
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «… اس کی مرمت کی گئی، اور اس کے ساتھ ساتھ سوق القیصریہ نامی بازار نئے سرے سے بنا اور دستکاروں کا بازار وجود میں آیا۔» in both leaves.
